newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish policemen protest against low wages.
newsitem.headline: Polish policemen protest against low wages.

text.p: More than 2,000 Polish policeman staged a rally on Tuesday demanding a 25 percent wage increase and more funds in next year's budget to replace their antiquated equipment.
The rally, outside the parliament building in downtown Warsaw, was part of a nationwide protest by the police section of the Solidarity trade union launched two weeks ago.

The union is demanding an average increase of 200 zlotys ($70) a month to bring the average monthly police salary to about 900 zlotys ($320), in line with the military, said police Solidarity official Zenon Trocha.
"Policemen, who risk their lives, must not find themselves in a situation in which they have to think all the time how to make ends meet," Trocha told Reuters.

He said that meeting demands of pay rises and more funds for equipment would require adding about 300 million zlotys ($106 million) to the 2.6 billion zlotys allotted for the police force in the 1997 budget draft.
Interior Minister Zbigniew Siemiatkowski, who was present at the rally, said he fully understood the demands, but he was whistled at in derision by the protesters.
PAP news agency quoted him as saying he had done all he could and that the decision on police spending now rested with parliament.
